newsitem.title: NORWAY: Storebrand may look abroad for partner.
newsitem.headline: Storebrand may look abroad for partner.

text.p: Norway's largest insurance company Storebrand ASA will look overseas for a possible merger partner following the aborted fusion with Christiania Bank og Kreditakasse ASA, according to the latest edition of Storebrand's in-house magazine Vi.
"One thing is certain. Such as the Norwegian financial market is, a merger with another Norwegian bank or a Norwegian insurance company is of no interest," the magazine said.
"A solution with a small, Norwegian commercial bank would not give enough strategic value and a merger with another Norwegian insurance company would not be possible with regards to competition."

Storebrand's plans to merge with Christiania Bank were blocked at an extraordinary shareholders meeting at the end of June. In a knife-edge vote, supporters of the deal won 62 percent of the ballot, but required a two-thirds majority to pass the plan.

The company's CEO, Aage Korsvol, interviewed in Vi, said the rejection was not a castrophe for the group. He would continue to work towards the strategies already put in place, and in the short term concentrate on growth alone rather than through a merger or acquisition.
In the longer term, the situation could be different but it was too early to say, Korsvold said.

"We have seen possiblities in other Nordic countries," he said, emphasising that there were no concrete plans. "An international acquisition of a company of the same size as Storebrand is extremely demanding. A restructuring with a similar (sized) partner is more likely."
